# Venue record: NeurIPS 2026, Main Track (contribution type "General")

Sources: `ht-role venue neurips` (the world's venue library, retrieved 2026-11-14 from neurips.cc pages and the official style kit) and, for contribution types, https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/ReviewerGuidelines (fetched 2026-11-25). ## 1. Choice of venue

The objective lets the study pick one of ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS and requires the newest edition's official template and checklist. I pick **NeurIPS 2026 Main Track** (newest NeurIPS edition with a published call; NeurIPS 2027 pages return HTTP 404 on 2026-11-14, so the edition and its template are the 2026 ones).

Why not the others (from the same library):

| | NeurIPS 2026 | ICML 2027 | ICLR 2027 |

| layout | one column, 5.5 in text width | two columns, 6.75 in text width, 3.25 in columns | one column, 5.5 in |

**Contribution type: choose "General"** (reviewers read criteria by the type the authors select; it cannot be changed after submission). "Negative Results" is for papers whose main contribution is understanding a negative result and has a *higher* significance and originality bar ("unexpected or surprising", "changes our understanding of an important question", and not "simply an empirical observation that some experiment did not turn out as expected"). The study's thesis (an extrapolation account of regression-GATE error, a regime map, a diagnostic) is evaluation-of-existing-methods work, which the General originality criterion names explicitly ("new insights, deepen understanding, or highlight important properties of existing methods"). - Main text: **at most 9 content pages, including all figures and tables**. Not counted: references, acknowledgments, technical appendices, the paper checklist. # Outline — what the paper says and what carries it (revision 3: review round 1 and Brief revision 5)

Source: `idea-repo` Brief revision 4 (the idea, the predictions P1–P5, the study design and cell budget), the objective (`story-repo`#1) and `prior_work.md`. This page says *what to test and where it shows*, never what a result must be. Every claim below has a "refuted if" line; a result that triggers it changes the claim, and I take it to `idea-repo` (see "When results do not carry it").

## 1. The story in one paragraph
Regression-adjustment estimators of the global average treatment effect (GATE) under network interference (Chin 2019; Han–Ugander 2023) fit outcome on functions of the assignment (own treatment, treated-neighbour fraction, …) and predict at all-treated and all-control. Published work shows they *can* work but gives no account of *how well, why, and when not*. We treat the estimator as **extrapolation from the observed exposure distribution to the two global corners** and ask what that predicts. The error splits into a **variance part** (OLS leverage of the corner contrast, scaling like d/(p(1−p)n)) and a **bias part** (curvature of the response × raw distance of the corner from the observed exposure support, roughly *not* growing with degree). The two parts have different drivers and, for the fraction feature, are predicted to move in opposite directions with degree (count, 2-hop and threshold mechanisms have their own predicted scalings), so "error grows with degree" is predicted to hold only where noise dominates. Abstract wording stays conditional until C2 is in. We test these scalings across interference mechanisms, graph families (synthetic and two real Facebook graphs), treatment probabilities and designs (Bernoulli, graph-cluster); map where regression beats and loses to difference-in-means (DM) and to exposure-mapping HT/Hájek; ask whether flexible/data-adaptive learners help; and test a data-computable two-part diagnostic against pre-registered trivial predictors. Not a new estimator: a verified, predictive account of when to trust an existing one. Positive, negative and mixed outcomes are all reported.

## 2. Position against prior work (Related work, one paragraph per cluster)
- *Regression GATE estimators*: Chin 2019 (estimator; Fig. 2 already shows the exposure-distribution mismatch qualitatively and draws the off-policy analogy), Han–Ugander 2023 (covariate generation/selection, block bootstrap). **We do not claim the extrapolation viewpoint as new**; we claim the quantified decomposition, its tests across mechanisms/graphs/designs, the regime map including where regression loses, and the diagnostic. - *Designs*: Karrer et al. 2021, Cortez et al. 2022 (optional), Chen et al. 2023, Leung 2022 rate. *Overlap/positivity*: Crump 2009, D'Amour 2021 (where the extrapolation analogy comes from).

shown.message:
I answered `figtab-repo` on `venue-repo`#2 and closed it. I also confirmed the venue budget to `story-repo` on `story-repo`#4. I pushed nothing, because `VENUE.md` already holds these facts.

- **Widths:** the text width is 5.5 in. NeurIPS 2026 is one column, so there is no separate column width. Figures may be at most 5.5 in wide and may not go into the margins. Two side-by-side panels are about 2.65 in each.
- **Page limit:** the main text is 9 pages including all figures and tables. References, appendix and checklist are outside it.
- **Type size:** the venue sets no minimum for text in figures. The style floors `\footnotesize` at 8 pt, `\scriptsize` at 7 pt and `\tiny` at 6 pt. I recommended at least 7 pt as printed, 8 pt preferred, and nothing smaller than 8 pt in tables. Captions print at the 10 pt body size.
- **Fonts:** Type 3 and non-embedded fonts get flagged. Matplotlib needs `pdf.fonttype: 42`.
- **Budget:** the outline's main-text proposal (Figs 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and Tables 1–2) fits. My cap is 6 figures plus 2 tables, so one multi-panel figure could carry Figs 2, 4, 6 and 8. The accepted-paper sample has at most 5 figures.

My first comment on `venue-repo`#2 had stray backslashes before the backticks. I edited the comment to remove them.
